questions.question_text: A glycoalkaloid [P] Contains sulphur in addition to nitrogen in its molecule [Q] Is glycosidic in nature. [R] Can be hydrolysed to an alkaloid. [S] Always contains endocyclic nitrogen in its molecule.
questions.explanation: Glycoalkaloids are glycosidic compounds containing a sugar moiety attached to an alkaloid aglycone, which can be liberated upon hydrolysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements are true for ginseng root [P] It is among the most traded plant material of Brazil [Q] It is obtained from Panax ginseng and Panax quinquefolium [R] It is obtained from young plants of six months to one year age [S] It contains derivatives of protopanaxadiol
questions.explanation: Ginseng is obtained from Panax species and contains ginsenosides which are derivatives of protopanaxadiol and protopanaxatriol.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs is a triterpenoid containing root?
questions.explanation: Shatavari contains steroidal saponins and triterpenoid roots.

questions.question_text: Which of the following alkaloids is derived from tyrosine
questions.explanation: Morphine is a benzylisoquinoline alkaloid derived biosynthetically from tyrosine.

questions.question_text: The following options carry the name of the plant, part used and its family. Find a wrong combination.

options.C: Glycyrrhiza glabra, root and stolon & Leguminosae

questions.explanation: Strophanthus gratus belongs to the family Apocynaceae, not Scrophulariaceae.

questions.question_text: Anomocytic stomata, trichomes with collapsed cell and absence of calcium oxalate crystals are some of the microscopic features of which plant
questions.explanation: Hyoscyamus leaves possess anomocytic stomata and glandular trichomes with multicellular stalks and collapsed heads.

questions.question_text: Each of the following options lists the name of the drug, its class, pharmacological action and plant source. Choose an option showing a wrong combination.
questions.explanation: Myrrh is obtained from Commiphora molmol or Commiphora abyssinica, whereas Commiphora wightii yields guggul.

questions.question_text: Quinoline alkaloids are biosynthesized via which one of the following pathways
questions.explanation: Quinoline alkaloids like quinine are derived from tryptophan and secologanin via the strictosidine pathway.

questions.question_text: Which of the following ergot alkaloids is water soluble and shows blue fluorescence
questions.explanation: Ergometrine (ergobasine) is the only water-soluble ergot alkaloid and exhibits blue fluorescence in solution.

questions.question_text: Khellin is an active constituent of which one of the following plants
questions.explanation: Khellin is a furanochromone obtained from the fruits of Ammi visnaga.

questions.question_text: Goldbeater's skin test is used to detect the presence of which one of the following classes of compounds
questions.explanation: Goldbeater's skin test is a standard qualitative assay for the detection of tannins.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following compounds is useful for the stimulation of cell division and release of lateral bud dormancy?
questions.explanation: Zeatin is a naturally occurring cytokinin that promotes cell division and breaks bud dormancy.

questions.question_text: Phenylethylisoquinoline is the precursor of which of the following alkaloids
questions.explanation: Colchicine is biosynthetically derived from phenylethylisoquinoline precursors.

questions.question_text: A powdered drug has the following microscopic characters: Anther cells, parenchyma, pollen grains, phloem fibers, volatile oil cells and stone cells. The powder is obtained from which of the followings?
questions.explanation: Phloem fibers and stone cells are characteristic of clove stalks, which contaminate clove bud powder when mixed.

questions.question_text: Arrange the following fatty acids in decreasing order of their unsaturation (highest to lowest) [P] Stearic [Q] Oleic acid [R] Linolenic acid [S] Linoleic acid
questions.explanation: Linolenic acid has 3 double bonds, linoleic has 2, oleic has 1, and stearic acid is saturated (0 double bonds).

questions.question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion (a): Tannins are polyphenolic substances occurring in plant cell sap. Hydrolysable and condensed tannins are differentiated by match stick test. Reason (r): The condensed tannins are resistant to acid hydrolysis therefore stain the lignin present in matchstick.

options.A: Both (a) and (r) are true, and (r) is a correct reason for (a)
options.B: Both (a) and (r) are true, but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)
options.C: (a) is true but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)

questions.explanation: Condensed tannins react with phloroglucinol-HCl in the matchstick test to produce a red color due to their reaction with lignin/phlobaphenes.

questions.question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion (a): Castor oil is soluble in alcohol and is used as purgative. Reason (r): The oil contains ricinoleic acid having a hydroxyl group at C-12 position which is responsible for its solubility in alcohol and its purgative action.

options.A: Both (a) and (r) are true but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)
options.B: (a) is true but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)
options.C: Both (a) and (r) are true and (r) is the correct reason for (a)

questions.explanation: The presence of the free hydroxyl group in ricinoleic acid imparts polarity, making castor oil soluble in alcohol and driving its irritant purgative action.

questions.question_text: In acetate mevalonate pathway geranyl pyrophosphate leads to formation of monoterpenes, the major constituents of volatile oils. [P] Geranyl pyrophosphate contains two isoprene units [Q] Monoterpenes have 15 carbon atoms [R] The two isoprene units condense in head to tail fashion to give Monoterpenes [S] Isoprene unit has molecular formula of $C_5H_8$. which one of the given statements is correct?

options.A: P is true, Q is false, R is true, S is false
options.B: P is false, Q is true, R is true, S is false
options.C: P is true, Q is true, R is false, S is true
options.D: P is true, Q is false, R is true, S is true

questions.explanation: Monoterpenes contain 10 carbons (two C5 units), so statement Q is false, while P, R, and S are correct.

questions.question_text: Two genetic types of Cannabis i.e. drug type and Hemp types are cultivated. [P] Drug type cannabis is rich in (-)$9$-trans-tetrahydrocannabinol [Q] Hemp type cannabis is rich in cannabidiol [R] Drug type cannabis is rich in cannabidiol [S] Hemp type cannabis contains elongated bast fibres which one of the given statements is correct?

options.A: P is true, Q is true, R is true, S is true
options.B: P is true, Q is true, R is false, S is true
options.C: P is true, Q is true, R is false, S is false
options.D: P is false, Q is true, R is false, S is true

questions.explanation: Drug-type cannabis is rich in psychoactive THC, whereas hemp-type is cultivated for fiber and is rich in CBD.

questions.question_text: Each of the following options lists a phytoconstituent, its phytochemical grouping, pharmacological activity and corresponding semisynthetic analogue. Find a MISMATCHING option
questions.explanation: Sinigrin is a glucosinolate found in mustard, not a semisynthetic analogue of sennoside.

questions.question_text: Inhibition/induction of which of the following Cytochrome P450 enzyme system ismost likely to be involved in important drug-drug interactions
questions.explanation: CYP3A4 is the most abundant hepatic CYP450 enzyme and metabolizes the largest share of clinically used drugs, making it primary for interactions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following mechanisms is NOT related to platelet aggregation inhibitory action
questions.explanation: Prostacyclin inhibits platelet aggregation; thus, prostacyclin inhibition would promote, not inhibit, platelet aggregation.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct statement about the given four diseases? [P] Cardiomyopathy [Q] Rheumatoid arthritis [R] Myasthenia gravis [S] Ulcerative colitis

options.C: P & R are not autoimmune disorders
options.D: R & S are not autoimmune disorders

questions.explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis and ulcerative colitis are well-known autoimmune disorders.

questions.question_text: Which of the following species is being inactivated by the enzyme Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4
questions.explanation: DPP-4 is the enzyme responsible for the rapid degradation of incretin hormones like GLP-1 and GIP.

questions.question_text: Patients taking isosorbide mononitrate or nitroglycerine should be advised not to take Sildenafil. This drug- drug interaction causes which of the following actions
questions.explanation: Combining nitrates with PDE5 inhibitors causes a synergistic rise in cGMP leading to profound, potentially fatal hypotension.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drugs does NOT induce mydriasis?
questions.explanation: Phentolamine is an alpha blocker that causes miosis rather than mydriasis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE for angiotensin-II

options.B: Decreases the action of sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Decreases the synthesis and release of aldosterone

questions.explanation: Angiotensin II promotes vascular and cardiac remodeling, including myocyte hypertrophy.

questions.question_text: Which of the following beta blockers has been shown clinically to reduce mortality in patients of symptomatic heart failure
questions.explanation: Carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol are proven to reduce mortality in heart failure.

questions.question_text: All of the given four drugs cause vasodilatation. Choose the correct statement about them. [P] Bradykinin [Q] Minoxidil [R] Acetylcholine [S] Hydralazine

options.A: P & Q cause release of nitric oxide
options.B: Q & R do not cause release of nitric oxide
options.C: R & S cause release of nitric oxide
options.D: P & S do not cause release of nitric oxide

questions.explanation: Bradykinin and minoxidil or endothelial-dependent pathways involve nitric oxide release for vasodilation.

questions.question_text: Rhabdomyolysis is the side effect associated with which of the following classes of drugs
questions.explanation: Statins are well-known to cause myopathy and rhabdomyolysis as a severe adverse effect.

questions.question_text: Blood level monitoring of HbA1c is important in which of the given diseased states
questions.explanation: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over the past 3 months and is the standard metric for monitoring diabetes mellitus.

questions.question_text: Most of the emergency contraceptives have which of the following active ingredients
questions.explanation: Levonorgestrel is the standard progestin used in emergency contraceptive pills (e.g., Plan B).

questions.question_text: Which of the following antibiotics produces concentration dependent bactericidal action and also possesses post-antibiotic effect
questions.explanation: Aminoglycosides like amikacin exhibit concentration-dependent killing and a significant post-antibiotic effect.

questions.question_text: Antiretroviral Raltegravir is unique, because of which of its following actions
questions.explanation: Raltegravir was the first HIV integrase strand transfer inhibitor approved for clinical use.

questions.question_text: What is chemotaxis
questions.explanation: Chemotaxis refers to the directional movement of cells (such as leucocytes) in response to chemical gradients during inflammation.

questions.question_text: Which one of the followings is NOT an example of G-protein coupled receptor?
questions.explanation: Nicotinic cholinergic receptors are ligand-gated ion channels, not G-protein coupled receptors.

questions.question_text: Which of the followings used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis is NOT a biologic response modifier
questions.explanation: Leflunomide is a conventional synthetic DMARD, whereas the others are biologic DMARDs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is FALSE for artemisinin?

options.A: It is a sesquiterpene lactone endoperoxide
options.B: It is a drug of choice in prophylaxis of malaria
options.C: It does not cure relapsing malaria
options.D: It is useful in treatment of cerebral falciparum malaria

questions.explanation: Artemisinins are not used for malaria prophylaxis due to their short half-life and to prevent resistance development.

questions.question_text: Which of the followings is a noncompetitive inhibitor of the enzyme reverse transcriptase in HIV
questions.explanation: Nevirapine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI), which acts as a noncompetitive inhibitor.

questions.question_text: Which of the followings is the most effective monotherapy for raising HDL cholesterol
questions.explanation: Niacin (nicotinic acid) remains the most effective pharmacologic agent for increasing HDL cholesterol levels.

questions.question_text: Which of the following parameters from plasma concentration time profile study gives indication of the rate of drug absorption?
questions.explanation: T_max is the time required to reach peak plasma concentration and reflects the rate of drug absorption.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pairs has high binding affinity for 5\alpha -reductase
questions.explanation: Finasteride is a competitive inhibitor of 5-alpha-reductase, and testosterone is the natural substrate with high affinity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following skeletal muscle relaxants acts directly on the contractile mechanism of the muscle fibers
questions.explanation: Dantrolene acts directly on skeletal muscle by blocking ryanodine receptors (RyR1), inhibiting calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

questions.question_text: Which is the molecular target for the vinca alkaloids as anticancer agents
questions.explanation: Vinca alkaloids bind to tubulin and inhibit the formation of microtubules, arresting cells in metaphase.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct pair of the neurodegenerative disorders from those given below.
questions.explanation: Both Parkinson's and Alzheimer's are characterized by progressive neurodegeneration.

questions.question_text: A 64 year old woman with a history of Type II diabetes is diagnosed with heart failure. Which of the followings would be a Poor choice in controlling her diabetes
questions.explanation: Thiazolidinediones like pioglitazone cause fluid retention and worsen or precipitate heart failure, making them contraindicated.

questions.question_text: Mifepristone and gemeprost combination is used for medical termination of pregnancy. The action is caused due to which of the following mechanisms

options.A: Mifepristone is an antiestrogen while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor agonist
options.B: Mifepristone is an antiprogestin while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor agonist
options.C: Mifepristone is an antiandrogen while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor agonist
options.D: Mifepristone is an antiprogestin while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor antagonist

questions.explanation: Mifepristone is a progesterone receptor antagonist (antiprogestin) and gemeprost is a PGE1 analogue that contracts the uterus.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following is a $\beta$ lactamase inhibitor
questions.explanation: Clavulanic acid is a well-known mechanism-based inhibitor of beta-lactamase enzymes.

questions.question_text: All of the followings are indications for use of ACE inhibitors Except for one. Identify that
questions.explanation: Pheochromocytoma is managed using alpha blockers (e.g., phenoxybenzamine), not ACE inhibitors.

questions.question_text: Neural tube defects may occur by which one of the following anti-seizure drugs
questions.explanation: Valproic acid is strongly associated with a high incidence of neural tube defects (like spina bifida) when taken during pregnancy.

questions.question_text: Which water is used for hand washing in a change room of pharmaceutical manufacturing plant?
questions.explanation: Potable (drinking) water is standard for washing hands prior to entering pharmaceutical processing areas.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following drying methods is commonly used in Pharma industry for dryingof soft shell capsules?
questions.explanation: Fluid bed drying is extensively used for the rapid and uniform drying of soft gelatin capsules.

questions.question_text: Which one of the followings does NOT afford a macromolecular inclusion compound
questions.explanation: Cyclodextrins form molecular inclusion complexes, whereas zeolites and dextrins/gels form larger channel or network lattices.

questions.question_text: If C is the concentration of dissolved drug and Cs is the saturation concentration. In which case the sink conditions are said to be maintained?
questions.explanation: Sink conditions are generally maintained when the concentration of the solute in the bulk solution is kept well below saturation, typically below 10% to 20% of Cs (often cited as < 10%-20% with < 10% being the stricter definition).

questions.question_text: Which condition does not apply as per Indian law while conducting single dose bioavailability study of an immediate release product

options.A: Sampling period should be at least three t_1/2 el
options.B: Sampling should represent pre-exposure, peak exposure and post-exposure phases
options.C: There should be at least four sampling points during elimination phase
options.D: Sampling should be continued till measured AUC is at least equal to 80% of AUC

questions.explanation: Typically, at least 3 to 4 points are needed in the terminal elimination phase, but specific regulatory guidance requires AUC truncation rules rather than exactly four points in elimination.

questions.question_text: Upon standing sometimes gel system shrinks a bit and little liquid is pressed out. What is this phenomenon, known as
questions.explanation: Syneresis is the contraction of a gel upon standing, with the consequent squeezing out of liquid.

questions.question_text: Which of the following routes of administration of drugs is associated with Phlebitis
questions.explanation: Phlebitis is inflammation of a vein, commonly associated with intravenous catheterization and IV drug administration.

questions.question_text: Study the following two statements and choose the correct answer: [P] Antibodies are serum proteins providing immunity. [Q] IgG provides immunity to new born babies while IgM is the first generated antibody.

options.A: P is correct and Q is incorrect
options.B: P is incorrect and Q is correct
options.C: Both P and Q are correct
options.D: Both P and Q are incorrect

questions.explanation: Both statements are immunologically accurate regarding antibody classes and functions.

questions.question_text: Which microbe is used for validation of sterilization by filtration process
questions.explanation: Pseudomonas diminuta (ATCC 19146) is the standard challenge microorganism used for membrane filter validation due to its small size (0.3 um).

questions.question_text: Non-linear pharmacokinetics can be expected due to [P] Enzyme induction [Q] Active secretion Choose the correct answer

options.A: Both P and Q are true
options.B: P is true, Q is false
options.C: Q is true, P is false
options.D: Both P and Q are false

questions.explanation: Both enzyme induction and active transport/secretion processes are known causes of non-linear (dose-dependent) pharmacokinetics.

questions.question_text: Which wavelength of the UV light provides maximum germicidal action
questions.explanation: Germicidal UV lamps typically emit around $253.7\text{ nm}$, which corresponds to the peak absorption of nucleic acids.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT

options.A: Chick Martin test uses organic matter in media
options.B: The organism in Rideal-walker test is S. typhi
options.C: Rideal-walker test uses organic matter in media
options.D: The organism in Chick Martin test is S. typhi

questions.explanation: Unlike the Chick Martin test, the Rideal-Walker test does not use organic matter in the testing medium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following forces contribute to stability of charge-transfer complexes

options.C: Dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces

questions.explanation: Charge-transfer complex stability involves resonance structures of the complex as well as London dispersion forces.

questions.question_text: Which of the following isotherms are produced when the heat of condensation of successive layers is more than the heat of adsorption of first layer
questions.explanation: Type III and V isotherms occur when adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are greater than adsorbent-adsorbate interactions.

questions.question_text: Which of the followings act as a non-ionic emulsifying agent
questions.explanation: Polysorbates (polyoxyethylene sorbitan fatty acid esters) are classic non-ionic surfactants.

questions.question_text: The minimal effective flow rate of air in laminar flow hood should be not less than how many cubic feet per minute
questions.explanation: Standard laminar airflow hoods require a velocity delivering approximately $100\text{ ft}^3/\text{min}$ ($\pm 20\%$) to maintain sterility.

questions.question_text: Which of the following Schedules include shelf life of drugs
questions.explanation: Schedule P of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act prescribes the life period (shelf-life) of drugs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following pumps is used in handling of corrosive liquids
questions.explanation: Peristaltic pumps isolate the fluid inside the tubing, making them ideal for corrosive or sterile liquids without pump contamination.

questions.question_text: By addition of which of the followings the shells of soft gelatin capsules may be made elastic
questions.explanation: Plasticizers such as sorbitol and glycerol are added to gelatin to impart flexibility and elasticity.

questions.question_text: Convert $90\%\text{ v/v}$ akohol to Proof strength. Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Proof strength $= (\% \text{v/v} \times 1.753) - 100$. For $90\%$, $(90 \times 1.753) - 100 = 157.77 - 100 = 57.77^{\circ}$ over proof.

questions.question_text: Department of Transport Test (DOT) is performed for which of the followings
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) leak test and pressure test are standard evaluations for aerosol containers.

questions.question_text: What is the Heat of vaporization of water at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$?
questions.explanation: The latent heat of vaporization of water at its boiling point is approximately $9720\text{ cal/mol}$ ($40.65\text{ kJ/mol}$).

questions.question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion[a]: For a pharmaceutical powder true density is greater than the granule density. Reason[r]: Mercury displacement used for determining granule density, allows penetration of liquid into internal pores of the particles.

options.C: Both [a] and [r] are true and [r] is the correct reason for [a]
options.D: Both [a] and [r] are true but [r] is NOT the correct reason for [a]

questions.explanation: True density accounts only for solid material volume, whereas granule density includes intraparticle pores; mercury does not penetrate internal pores at low pressures, making reason [r] false.

questions.question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following statements: [P] Rheopexy is the phenomenon when a sols form gel more readily when sheared gently. [Q] In a rheopectic system, sol is the equilibrium form. [R] Rheopexy is a phenomenon when a sol forms gel when the material is kept at rest

options.A: [R] is true but [P] and [Q] are false
options.B: [P] is true but [Q] and [R] are false

questions.explanation: Rheopexy describes a system that solidifies/gels more quickly when gently shaken or sheared, making P true and R false.

questions.question_text: Define Plasmapheresis. Choose the correct answer

options.A: The process of collecting plasma and returning the red blood cells concentrate to the donor
options.B: The process of collecting red blood cells concentrate and returning the plasma to the donor
options.C: The process of separating whiteblood cells from blood
options.D: The process of generating artificial blood plasma expanders

questions.explanation: Plasmapheresis involves extracting plasma from drawn blood and returning the cellular components back to the donor.

questions.question_text: Molecules in the smectic liquid crystals are characterized by which one of the followings

options.A: Mobility in three directions and rotation in one axis
options.B: Mobility in two directions and rotation in one axis
options.C: Mobility in two directions and no rotation
options.D: Mobility in three directions and no rotation

questions.explanation: Smectic liquid crystals have layered structures where molecules maintain translational mobility in two directions and can rotate about their long axis.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct sequence of Moisture vapor Transmission Rate in packaging materials?
questions.explanation: Paper has the highest moisture vapor transmission rate (MVTR), whereas aluminum foil has virtually zero (lowest).

questions.question_text: How many $\text{mL}$ of $50\%\text{ (w/v)}$ dextrose solution and how many $\text{mL}$ of $5\%\text{ (w/v)}$ dextrose solution are required to prepare $4500\text{ mL}$ of a $10\%\text{ (w/v)}$ solution?
questions.explanation: Using alligation: parts of $50\% = 5$, parts of $5\% = 40$. Ratio is $5:40$ ($1:8$). Total 9 parts = $4500\text{ mL}$, so 1 part ($50\%$) = $500\text{ mL}$ and 8 parts ($5\$) = $4000\text{ mL}$.

questions.question_text: A drug is administered to a $65\text{ Kg}$ patient as $500\text{ mg}$ tablets every $4\text{ hours}$. Half-life of the drug is $3\text{ h}$, volume of distribution is $2\text{ liter/Kg}$ and oral bioavailability of the drug is $0.85$. Calculate the steady state concentration of the drug
questions.explanation: Css = $(F \times Dose) / (Cl \times \tau)$. Calculation yields approximately $5.05\text{ mcg/ml}$.

questions.question_text: P-Glycoprotein pump is responsible for which one of the followings

options.A: Transporting the drugs from the enterocytes into the gutlumen
options.B: Transporting the drugs from gut lumen into enterocytes
options.C: Transporting the drugs from oral mucosa into blood capillaries
options.D: Transporting the drugs from Peyer's patches into the gut lumen

questions.explanation: P-glycoprotein acts as an efflux pump, pumping xenobiotics and drugs out of enterocytes back into the intestinal lumen.

questions.question_text: Statement [x]: Hofmeister series grades coagulating power of electrolytes as per their ionic size. Statement [y]: Their relative coagulating power is given by: [P] $\text{Al}^{3+} > \text{Ba}^{2+}$ [Q] $\text{Li} > \text{F}$ [R] $\text{NH}^+_4 > \text{Na}^+$ Choose the correct statement:

options.A: Statement x is true but P, Q and R are false in Statement Y
options.B: Statement x is false and P, Q and R are false in Statement Y
options.C: Statement x is true and Q and R are false in Statement Y
options.D: Statement x is false and P is false in Statement

questions.explanation: Hofmeister series is based on ion hydration and kosmotropic/chaotropic properties, not strictly ionic size alone, and valence rules apply (Schulze-Hardy rule).

questions.question_text: The first stage of wetting on addition of a granulating agent to the powders is characterized by which one of the followings?
questions.explanation: In the initial wetting stage with low liquid saturation, the pendular state is formed where liquid bridges exist at particle contact points.

questions.question_text: Larger values of Ky in the Heckel Plot indicate formation of what quality of tablets?
questions.explanation: A larger Heckel constant $k$ (or $K_y$) reflects higher plasticity and lower yield strength, often corresponding to softer or more readily deformable materials.

questions.question_text: The degree of flocculation of a suspension is $1.5$ and the sedimentation volume is $0.75$. What will be the ultimate volume of deflocculated suspension
questions.explanation: Degree of flocculation $\beta = F / F_\infty$. Thus $F_\infty = 0.75 / 1.5 = 0.5$.

questions.question_text: What will be the time required for a drug exhibiting first order rate constant of $4.6/\text{hr}$ to be degraded from initial concentration of $100\text{ mg/ml}$ to $10\text{ mg/ml}$?
What will be the dose required maintaining therapeutic concentration of $20\text{ }\mu\text{gm/ml}$ for $24\text{ hr}$ of a drug exhibiting total clearance of $2\text{ L/hr}$?
questions.explanation: Total Dose = $C_p \times Cl \times t = 20\text{ }\mu\text{g/mL} \times 2000\text{ mL/hr} \times 24\text{ hr} = 960,000\text{ }\mu\text{g} = 960\text{ mg}$.

questions.question_text: What will be the urine to plasma ratio of a weakly acidic drug having pKa of $5$? [urine $(\text{pH} : 5)$ plasma $(\text{pH} : 7)$]
questions.explanation: For a weak acid, $U/P = (1 + 10^{\text{pH}_u - \text{pKa}}) / (1 + 10^{\text{pH}_p - \text{pKa}}) = (1 + 10^{5-5}) / (1 + 10^{7-5}) = 2 / 101 \approx 1:50.5$ or closer to $1:101$ derivation based on ionized fractions.

questions.question_text: The Reynolds number widely used to classify flow behavior of fluids is the ratio of which one of the followings:
questions.explanation: Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces within a fluid.

questions.question_text: If the distillation graph using McCabe Thiele method is parallel to x-axis, then the feed is which one of the followings?
questions.explanation: In McCabe-Thiele analysis, a feed line slope of zero (q = 0, parallel to x-axis) represents a saturated vapor feed.

questions.question_text: What for the baffles are provided in a shell and tube heat exchanger?
questions.explanation: Baffles direct fluid flow across the tube bundle, increasing turbulence and heat transfer efficiency.

questions.question_text: SOS means which one of the followings
questions.explanation: The Latin abbreviation 'si opus sit' (SOS) means 'if necessary' or 'as needed'.

questions.question_text: Which statement is FALSE for Association Colloids
questions.explanation: Association colloids (micelles) form via hydrophobic association and are typically solvated at their hydrophilic outer shells, making 'partial solvation' an inaccurate distinguishing false statement.

questions.question_text: Which of the followings is NOT a reciprocating pump
questions.explanation: Gear pumps are rotary positive displacement pumps, not reciprocating pumps.

questions.question_text: Which is NOT applicable to protein binding
questions.explanation: Detli plot is not a standard linearization method for protein-ligand binding analysis (unlike Klotz, Scatchard, or Hill plots).

questions.question_text: Statement [P]: Soft gelatin capsules contain 12-15 % moisture. Statement [Q]: Hard gelatin capsule shells contain 6-10 % moisture. Choose the correct statement?

options.A: Both of the above statements P&Q are true
options.B: Both of the above statements P&Q are false
options.C: Statement P is true and Q is false
options.D: Statement P is false and Q is true

questions.explanation: Hard capsules typically contain 13-16% (often cited around 10-15%) or soft capsules contain higher moisture; standard reference values align both statements as generally accepted specifications.

questions.question_text: According to USP, the speed regulating device of the dissolution apparatus should be capable of maintaining the speed within limits of what % of the selected speed?
questions.explanation: USP specifications state that the rotation speed must be maintained within $\pm 5\%$ of the specified rate.

questions.question_text: A drug whose solubility is $1\text{ g/L}$ in water; when given orally at a dose of $500\text{ mg}$ is absorbed up to $95\%$ of the administered dose. The drug belongs to which class according to the BCS classification?
questions.explanation: Dose = $500\text{ mg} = 0.5\text{ g}$. Solubility = $1\text{ g/L}$, so volume required to dissolve dose is $500\text{ mL}$ ($< 250\text{ mL}$ threshold is high solubility if dose/solubility volume $\le 250\text{ mL}$). Since absorption is $95\%$, it is high permeability, placing it in BCS Class I.

questions.question_text: Which statement is NOT true for steam distillation

options.A: It is also called differential distillation
options.B: It can be used for separation of immiscible liquids

questions.question_text: Arrange the following Lowry-Bronsted acids into their decreasing order of acidity (highest to lowest) [P] $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ [Q] $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$ [R] $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ [S] $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$

questions.question_text: Alkenes show typical electrophilic addition reactions. If an electron withdrawing group is attached to one of the carbons bearing the double bond, what will happen to the mechanism of the addition reaction
questions.explanation: Strong electron-withdrawing groups on an alkene deplete electron density, shifting the pathway toward nucleophilic addition reactions.

questions.question_text: Aprotic polar solvents increase the rate of SN2 reactions manifold. Enhancement in the rate of such reactions is due to which one of the following effects

options.B: Solvation of both of the ionic species
options.C: Desolvation of the cation and solvation of the anion
options.D: Solvation of the cation by the solvent leaving the anion unaffected

questions.explanation: Polar aprotic solvents selectively solvate cations while leaving nucleophilic anions bare (unsolvated), greatly enhancing their nucleophilicity in SN2 reactions.

questions.question_text: Five-membered heteroaromatic compounds show a much higher rate of electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions than the six-membered ones. This is due to which one of the following reasons?

options.A: Five-membered heteroaromatic compounds have higher circulating electron density in the ring than the six-membered ones
options.B: Five-membered heteroaromatic compounds have lower circulating electron density in the ring than the six-membered ones
options.C: Five-membered rings are smaller in size than the six membered ones which affects their reaction rates
options.D: Six membered heteroaromatic rings are flat while the five-membered ones are puckered

questions.explanation: Five-membered heteroaromatic rings have 6 $\pi$ electrons distributed over 5 atoms, giving them a higher electron density per carbon compared to six-membered rings.

questions.question_text: Pyridine is more basic than pyrrole. This is due to which of the following facts

options.A: Lone pair of electrons on N in pyrrole is localized
options.B: Lone pair of electrons on N in pyridine is localized
options.C: Nitrogen of pyrrole has one hydrogen atom attached to it while pyridine does not haveany
options.D: Pyridine has three double bonds while pyrrole has only two

questions.explanation: In pyridine, the nitrogen lone pair resides in an $sp^2$ orbital perpendicular to the aromatic $\pi$ system and is localized (available for protonation), whereas pyrrole's lone pair is part of the aromatic sextet.
